A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 14 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including Appendices A–C, provide readable text, equations and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction examples, runtime measurements, statistical-query demonstrations and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds next-view selection comparisons, collision-probability sensitivity and further runtime results.

M1.justification: Section 3 now explicitly offers direct posterior mean/covariance inference alongside v1's sampling route. Next-view scoring also replaces the exact 0/1 endpoint test with an epsilon cutoff. The underlying Fourier reconstruction, pathwise sampling and cross-covariance amortization remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The mesh collection and reconstruction, collision-detection, hitbox, ray-casting and next-view-planning tasks are retained. The added next-view comparison and size sweeps deepen evaluation within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds randomly chosen views as a comparator in Figure 8 and a mean-only, non-stochastic PSR timing reference in Appendix C. SPSR remains the main reconstruction baseline, and the existing SGD-versus-Cholesky comparison is retained.

E3.justification: New evaluations compare selected versus random views using reported reconstruction errors and sweep collision-query data size and output size. Existing kernel, Fourier truncation, amortization-grid and hardware settings are retained. The new error metric and averaging protocol are not adequately specified.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds collision probability versus data size. Appendix C's Figure 15 extends the earlier input-size runtime analysis with an output-size sweep. Existing Fourier truncation, amortization density, solver-convergence and length-scale analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's new average-error labels do not establish a changed statistical reporting procedure; predictive surface uncertainty was already central to v1.

E6.justification: New Figure 8 reports initial error 0.096, average error 0.066 for random views and 0.060 for selected views. Appendix C adds mean-only PSR timings of 0.053, 0.54 and 9.1 seconds, alongside new sensitivity curves. These are additional results; the existing SPSR/Cholesky/SGD timing comparison is retained.

T1.justification: The stated cross-covariance assembly cost changes from O(LMNP) to O(LMN), and Equations 14–15 formalize the thresholded next-view score. The two main propositions, smoothness assumptions and Appendix A proof arguments remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The first contribution expands from producing posterior samples to explicitly producing means, covariances and samples. The abstract removes its direct claim of improved reconstruction quality. The central claims of one-solve reconstruction, local evaluation and independence from volumetric discretization remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the description of SPSR samples as non-smooth with an explanation that their smoothness comes from the Poisson solve, and qualifies its inability to answer correlation-dependent queries. Appendix B newly discusses small-length-scale kernel instability. The existing real-time computation limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository link and adds a Matérn-3/2 numerical-stability discussion, including the statement that its implementation uses an unnormalized expression. Existing software, hardware, mesh-source and principal hyperparameter disclosures remain. The linked resource was not accessed.

R1.justification: The same 33 references are retained. Research positioning is locally refined through the more qualified comparison with SPSR's correlation handling and the acknowledgment of smoothness supplied by its Poisson solve.

P1.justification: There are localized revisions to the abstract, contribution list, method explanation and baseline discussion. Section 3 drops 'Sampling-based' from its title, and the placeholder running header and publication information are updated. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 8, extends Figures 7 and 15 with new plots, and adjusts several figure labels, sizes and arrangements. Existing figures are mostly retained and renumbered, while a long Appendix A equation is wrapped across lines. The overall document format remains similar.

improvement.justification: The added next-view comparison and scaling evidence modestly strengthen empirical support, while the code link, implementation discussion and more qualified SPSR claims improve documentation. These gains are limited: Figure 8's error metric and averaging procedure are unspecified, Equation 14 conflicts with the retained transmittance sign convention, and Equation 32 has an apparent length-scale omission in its exponential rescaling.
